title: Improve downstream PostgreSQL test-suite performance
description:
## Verified audit

Audited git HEAD: 6edc72c. The worktree was clean before issue creation, Beads had no open work, and bv reported no duplicate suggestions.

Current evidence:
- Disposable creation and cleanup each open a new admin connection; every AdminClient builds a private Tokio runtime.
- Repeated template acquisition retains one shared-lock session per caller instead of caching a live per-server template.
- Explicit cleanup blocks the caller, while Drop fallback uses one process-global serial worker and retains the database permit until DROP finishes.
- Default capacity is floor(120 / 11) = 10 simultaneous database leases.
- Owned containers already disable fsync, synchronous_commit, and full_page_writes, but do not use initdb --no-sync or tmpfs.
- Testcontainers is always compiled, including external-server-only consumers.

Directional local measurements on cached postgres:18, Docker overlay2, 64 logical CPUs:
- 40 template0 create/comment/drop lifecycles: 1.16 s on one admin session versus 4.49 s with fresh create and cleanup sessions.
- pgbench SELECT: 0.156 ms persistent versus 9.13 ms reconnecting each transaction.
- Final TCP readiness: median 1.829 s current versus 1.306 s with initdb --no-sync.
- Twelve clone/drop cycles from a 40.5 MB template: 984 ms on the normal Docker volume versus 778 ms on tmpfs.
- FILE_COPY was slightly slower than default WAL_LOG for that template and is not accepted as a default optimization.

Accepted work tracks are the child issues. Explicit non-goals are enabling Testcontainers reusable-container mode, making trust authentication the default, weakening database-per-test isolation, or forcing FILE_COPY. Reduced-fidelity PostgreSQL settings require opt-in semantics and benchmark evidence.

## Success criteria

The project has reproducible performance characterization, fewer repeated setup costs, bounded cleanup and prewarming, a faster owned-container path, an external-only build, and actionable downstream guidance without weakening lifecycle safety.
acceptance_criteria: Every verified child is completed or closed with an evidence-backed rejection; benchmark results are recorded; database isolation, cleanup safety, and default public API behavior remain explicit.
close_reason: Completed all performance children with recorded benchmark evidence, preserved database isolation and cleanup safety, verified default public API compatibility, and passed the full default/external-only/MSRV/docs/package/Docker suite.

title: PERF02: Reuse a bounded pool of disposable-lifecycle admin sessions
description:
## Verified finding

src/harness.rs creates a fresh admin connection for every disposable database at create_test_database and another in DatabaseLeaseInner::cleanup. connect_admin constructs an AdminClient, and AdminClient::connect builds a private current-thread Tokio runtime, performs TCP and PostgreSQL authentication, spawns the connection task, and configures session timeouts.

Directional measurements:
- 40 template0 create/comment/drop lifecycles took 1.16 s using one session and 4.49 s using fresh create and cleanup sessions.
- pgbench averaged 0.156 ms per SELECT on a persistent connection and 9.13 ms when reconnecting each transaction.

The exact speedup inside Rust must be established by PERF01, but repeated connection and runtime construction is confirmed.

## Target

Add a lazy, bounded admin-session pool owned by ServerInner for disposable CREATE-COMMENT and DROP operations. Size it from an explicit policy tied to lifecycle concurrency and PostgreSQL headroom. Checkouts must be exclusive without holding the pool mutex during SQL work.

Keep retained owner and template advisory-lock sessions outside the reusable pool. Restore required session timeout state before reuse. Evict and replace sessions after protocol, connection, or uncertain session-state failures. Do not serialize all database creation and cleanup through one client.

## Guardrails and validation

Preserve create/tag compensation, detached spawn_blocking result cleanup, operation timeout errors, owned shutdown admission, and external mode. Add tests for reuse, pool bounds, concurrent progress, backend termination and reconnection, cancellation, poisoned-session eviction, and shutdown. Use pg_stat_activity or connection instrumentation to prove the pool bound and PERF01 to compare throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Disposable CREATE-COMMENT and DROP operations reuse a lazy bounded per-server admin-session pool; concurrency is not globally serialized; broken sessions are evicted; timeout and cancellation semantics are preserved; integration tests and the performance benchmark demonstrate lower connection churn.
close_reason: Implemented lazy bounded per-server lifecycle admin-session pooling with timeout reset, failure eviction/reconnection, concurrent pg_stat_activity coverage, shutdown/cancellation preservation, and PERF01 evidence of 93.75% lower lifecycle connection churn.

title: PERF03: Single-flight and cache live templates per server
description:
## Verified finding

Every PostgresHarness::template call runs begin_template through spawn_blocking and opens a retained PersistentClient. Even when the same fingerprint is already live in the same ServerInner, a new TemplateInner and shared advisory-lock session are created.

The integration suite confirms eight concurrent callers initialize once but deliberately expects eight additional ShareLock sessions. DatabaseTemplate::clone itself already shares one Arc and is cheap, so repeated template() calls are the avoidable path.

## Target

Add a per-ServerInner, fingerprint-keyed successful-template cache with single-flight initialization. Same-fingerprint callers in one server should await one initialization and receive handles backed by the same TemplateInner. Use weak ownership or another cycle-free design so cache state does not keep the server or template alive unintentionally.

On initializer error or cancellation, remove or transition the in-flight entry so a later caller can recover and use its own initializer. Preserve PostgreSQL advisory-lock coordination between distinct ServerInner values and processes.

## Guardrails and validation

Characterize and update N-way cold start, queued exclusive waiter fairness, initializer error recovery, initializer cancellation recovery, separate template-wait timeout behavior, shared-lock release after the final clone, and owned shutdown. Add warm-path assertions for one retained session and no extra catalog/lock round trips. Compare cold and warm acquisition with PERF01.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent and repeated same-fingerprint calls on one ServerInner share one live TemplateInner and retained shared-lock session; only one initializer runs; failure and cancellation cannot strand cache state; cross-server advisory-lock coordination and template lifetime safety remain covered.
close_reason: Completed per-server single-flight live-template cache with weak lifetime ownership, recovery regressions, cross-server lock validation, and PERF01 comparison

title: PERF04: Add bounded deferred cleanup with an explicit drain barrier
description:
## Verified finding

DatabaseLease::cleanup waits for a new admin connection and FORCE DROP before returning. DatabaseLease::drop sends DatabaseLeaseInner to one process-global DATABASE_CLEANUP_WORKER, which cleans every server and project serially. The OwnedSemaphorePermit remains inside DatabaseLeaseInner until cleanup finishes, so queued database requests cannot proceed even after the consumer has closed its application pool and returned the lease.

This is a confirmed critical-path and head-of-line-blocking seam. Any change must retain observable cleanup failures and bound residual databases.

## Target

Introduce a bounded, server-scoped deferred cleanup facility using the pooled admin sessions from PERF02. Provide an explicit asynchronous drain or shutdown barrier that waits for queued work and reports failures. Preserve the current awaited cleanup path for callers that require immediate confirmation; add a clearly named deferred return path or documented policy rather than silently discarding errors.

Define when the per-database connection permit is released. The contract may release it when a consumer explicitly returns the lease after closing all application pools, but must bound cleanup concurrency and queued residual databases so PostgreSQL connection and storage limits cannot be overrun.

## Guardrails and validation

Cover explicit success and failure, deferred success and failure reporting, queue saturation/backpressure, multiple harnesses, cancellation, Drop fallback, owned shutdown, external server lifetime, active application connections, permit handoff, and process teardown. No database may be reused without being recreated from the immutable template. PERF01 must record caller latency and final drain time.
acceptance_criteria: The harness offers bounded server-scoped deferred cleanup and an awaited drain that reports failures; cleanup is not globally serialized; database permits and shutdown ordering follow a documented safe contract; explicit cleanup behavior remains available and all lifecycle tests pass.
close_reason: Completed: added bounded server-scoped deferred cleanup, cancellation-safe drain/error reporting, documented permit and shutdown contracts, PERF01 timings, and full lifecycle coverage.

title: PERF05: Add opt-in prewarmed disposable database queues
description:
## Verified finding

Each DatabaseTemplate::database call synchronously acquires permits and performs CREATE DATABASE from the immutable template before returning a URL. For short downstream tests, the measured clone floor can dominate the test body even after admin sessions are pooled.

PostgreSQL has no portable constant-time snapshot or safe generic reset for arbitrary pools and extensions. Precreating clean clones and replacing returned databases is feasible without weakening database-level isolation.

## Target

Add an opt-in, bounded prewarmed queue associated with a DatabaseTemplate or a new pool abstraction. Prewarm clean databases from the template, hand out only never-used clones, and after return drop the dirty database and create a fresh replacement in the background.

Idle prewarmed databases must not hold application-connection permits. Acquire capacity atomically when leasing; retain the idle database if admission is closed or unavailable. Bound ready, creating, and deleting counts to cap disk or tmpfs consumption.

## Guardrails and validation

Never truncate and reuse a dirty database. Preserve unique names, metadata tagging, cancellation compensation, external stale-cleanup safety, template shared-lock lifetime, and owned shutdown. Test refill failures, queue exhaustion, concurrent leases, cancellation, multiple templates, drain behavior, and resource bounds. PERF01 must report first-lease latency, steady-state latency, refill throughput, and storage growth.
acceptance_criteria: An opt-in bounded prewarm API can prepare clean databases per template, lease them without reusing dirty state, refill after return, and shut down without leaked resources; idle databases do not consume application-connection permits; benchmark results quantify latency and storage tradeoffs.
close_reason: Completed bounded per-template prewarm queues with atomic lease admission, never-reused dirty returns, background refill, explicit/owned shutdown drains, slot accounting, cancellation and refill-failure coverage, schema-v8 benchmark measurements, and documented storage/latency tradeoffs.

title: PERF06: Add a fast and reliable owned-container storage profile
description:
## Verified finding

Owned containers currently pass fsync=off, synchronous_commit=off, full_page_writes=off, and max_connections=300, but do not set POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS or mount PostgreSQL storage on tmpfs.

The Docker Official postgres image supports POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS. PostgreSQL 18 documents initdb --no-sync as useful for testing. Testcontainers 0.27.3 exposes Mount::tmpfs_mount and ImageExt::with_mount. PostgreSQL 18's official image uses /var/lib/postgresql as the declared volume parent.

Local final-TCP-ready medians:
- current: 1.829 s;
- initdb --no-sync: 1.306 s, about 29 percent faster;
- no-sync plus tmpfs: 1.327 s, so tmpfs did not further improve startup.

For a 40.5 MB template, twelve clone/drop cycles took 984 ms on the normal volume and 778 ms on tmpfs, about 21 percent faster.

## Target

Add a coherent owned-container performance profile. Enable or expose initdb --no-sync for compatible owned images. Add configurable tmpfs storage with an explicit size cap and opt-out. Ensure readiness represents the final TCP-listening server, not the temporary server used by the image during initialization.

Treat --no-data-checksums, wal_level=minimal, and similar behavior-reducing settings as separate opt-ins unless representative benchmarks and compatibility tests justify them. Preserve custom-image support with documented capability expectations.

## Guardrails and validation

Test default and custom images, rootless or unsupported tmpfs behavior, memory exhaustion reporting, startup timeout cleanup, final readiness, container removal, and external mode unaffectedness. Record cold startup, migration, clone, and cleanup results through PERF01. Do not enable reusable-container mode or trust authentication by default.
acceptance_criteria: Owned-container startup supports verified initdb no-sync and bounded tmpfs configuration with reliable final-server readiness; defaults and opt-ins are documented; custom images and reduced-fidelity settings have explicit compatibility behavior; Docker lifecycle tests and benchmarks pass.
close_reason: Completed: added the default no-sync plus bounded-tmpfs owned profile, final TCP readiness and cleanup diagnostics, custom/external compatibility coverage, documentation, and schema-v5 benchmark evidence

title: PERF07: Characterize and expose effective database concurrency
description:
## Verified finding

HarnessConfig defaults to a connection budget of 120 and 11 permits per database, yielding ten simultaneous leases. The owned server separately hard-codes max_connections=300. Owner locks, template locks, lifecycle admin sessions, and external-server limits are not represented in a user-visible effective concurrency value.

The existing setters correctly enforce positive, order-independent overrides, but downstream users must infer lease parallelism and total their application pools manually.

## Target

Use PERF01 after admin pooling, template caching, and cleanup changes to characterize throughput across lease concurrency and downstream pool sizes. Expose the resolved budget, per-database permits, and effective maximum simultaneous leases through a stable read-only API or startup diagnostics.

Document that per-database permits cover the sum of all pools one test can open, and distinguish idle pool limits from actual eager connections. Evaluate whether owned max_connections should be derived from the configured budget plus explicit owner, template, admin-pool, and safety headroom. Change defaults only if representative results show a robust improvement.

## Guardrails and validation

Preserve 0 < per_database <= budget, builder order independence, terminal admission on owned shutdown, and external-server configurability. Test low-capacity servers, many templates, pool checkout spikes, superuser-reserved slots, and configurations larger than the owned server can safely support.
acceptance_criteria: Effective lease concurrency and its connection-pool formula are observable and documented; defaults or owned max_connections change only with benchmark evidence and explicit administrative headroom; existing configuration invariants and external-server safety remain tested.
close_reason: Completed stable resolved ConnectionLimits API, schema-v7 lease/pool spike characterization, owned and low-capacity external evidence, capacity documentation, and invariant/safety regressions.

title: PERF08: Feature-gate owned-container support for external-only builds
description:
## Verified finding

testcontainers is an unconditional normal dependency with blocking, ring, and watchdog features. A normal dependency-tree inspection found about 234 unique package-version entries beneath testcontainers. External-server consumers still compile this path even though ServerInner selects it only when no admin URL is configured.

Feature gating is feasible but not mechanical: src/server.rs contains all Testcontainers and libc::atexit use, while the public non-exhaustive Error enum exposes testcontainers::TestcontainersError in two variants. Default-feature API compatibility therefore needs explicit validation.

## Target

Introduce a default-enabled owned-container feature, with a clear name such as containers. Make testcontainers and container-only libc usage optional. With default features, preserve current behavior and public API. With owned-container support disabled, POSTGRES_TEST_ADMIN_URL or with_admin_database_url must work fully, while an attempt to start without an external URL returns a precise configuration error.

Decide and document the feature-specific shape of container error variants, HarnessConfig::with_image, container_id, and shutdown. Prefer keeping source compatibility in default builds.

## Guardrails and validation

Run cargo check, tests, rustdoc, MSRV, and public-API comparison under default features. Run check, tests, docs, and a real external PostgreSQL lifecycle under no-default-features. Prove through cargo tree that testcontainers, Bollard, Rustls/Ring pulled only by the container path, and container-only libc are absent where possible. Measure clean compile impact through PERF01.
acceptance_criteria: Default features preserve owned-container behavior and public API compatibility; a documented external-only build excludes testcontainers and container-only dependencies, requires an admin URL with a clear error otherwise, and passes check, tests, docs, and dependency-tree verification.
close_reason: Completed default-enabled containers feature, external-only lifecycle/error contract, dependency and clean-compile evidence, dual-mode CI/docs/MSRV validation, and exact default public-API comparison.

title: PERF09: Publish a downstream test-suite performance guide and adapter
acceptance_criteria: Documentation includes a tested reusable adapter and CI examples covering one harness and template per process, one external server per job, stable fingerprints, pool and permit sizing, cleanup and drain semantics, performance profiles, external-only builds, and explicit unsafe non-recommendations.
close_reason: Published and validated the downstream performance guide, executable OnceCell adapter with fingerprint and pool-geometry tests, real owned/external runs, and a one-service external-only CI job with explicit safety guidance.

title: Move UUID v4 support out of normal dependencies
description: The library uses UUID v7 in src, while UUID v4 is used only by examples and integration tests. Enabling the v4 feature in the normal dependency expands the published library's feature and transitive compile surface unnecessarily.
acceptance_criteria: The normal uuid dependency enables only features required by library code; examples and tests retain UUID v4 through dev-only configuration, and both feature matrices remain green.

Deliver DatabaseTemplate::derive(spec, initializer), returning an existing
immutable DatabaseTemplate built from a sealed parent plus a fingerprinted
local initialization step. Compose complete parent identity with local step

title: Stable composed template identity
description:
Delivery epic: postgres-test-harness-j82.

# Stable composed template identity

Type: task.
Priority: 1.
Depends on: none.
Unblocks: DT2 (postgres-test-harness-j82.2).
Primary file: `src/fingerprint.rs`.

Deliver a crate-private `derived_fingerprint(parent, step)` using the existing
SHA-256 dependency and opaque `TemplateFingerprint` representation.
Hash three frames in order: ASCII
`postgres-test-harness-derived-template-v1`, full 32-byte parent identity,
and full 32-byte local step identity.
Each frame is `u64` big-endian byte length followed by bytes.
Do not include the root builder's initial domain in this derived recipe.
Do not change root `FingerprintBuilder` output.

The composition is the persisted derived-cache contract.
It must distinguish changed parents and changed local steps and must propagate
an ancestor change when composed again for a grandchild.
Use full raw fingerprints rather than shortened hex or database names.
No new public fingerprint constructor is required.
No Cargo dependency changes are required.

Add unit coverage for an independently calculated golden vector, stable
repeated inputs, changed parent, changed step, swapped parent/step roles,
grandchild propagation, and preservation of the existing root golden vector.
The expected vector must be a fixed literal derived from documented framing,
not a value calculated with the production function during the test.
Use parent bytes `00` through `1f` and step bytes `20` through `3f`.
The expected child is
`678f8b338e81a48db8625fd8ab6c949a2852e6aec6261d710976de68381b7cd5`.

Acceptance:

- The helper's byte contract is documented next to its implementation.
- Existing root tests retain their expected values.
- Composition tests pass with default and disabled default features.
- No raw fingerprint representation becomes public.
- The diff is limited to identity implementation, documentation, and tests.

Validation:

```console
cargo test --locked --lib fingerprint
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --lib fingerprint
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

Why this precedes DT2 (postgres-test-harness-j82.2):
the complete child identity determines every cache key, database name,
metadata record, and advisory lock used by derivation.
Settling it first prevents incompatible intermediate identities.

## V01 — Independent fingerprint vector

Owner: DT1 (postgres-test-harness-j82.1).
Setup: parent bytes `00` through `1f`, step bytes `20` through `3f`.
Action: calculate the derived identity with the implementation.
Oracle: compare it with a literal SHA-256 digest calculated independently from
the exact three framed inputs in section 5.
Also retain the baseline root-vector assertion.
Failure detected: accidental root-domain reuse, hex encoding instead of raw
bytes, missing length prefix, field reordering, or root compatibility drift.

## V02 — Changed inputs and ancestry

Owner: DT1 (postgres-test-harness-j82.1), with database-level confirmation in DT2 (postgres-test-harness-j82.2).
Setup: two parent identities and two local step identities.
Action: compose each relevant pair and then apply a fixed grandchild step.
Oracle: identical pairs remain stable; changed parent or step produces a
different child; changed child changes the grandchild.
Failure detected: ignoring the parent, using a shortened fingerprint, or
returning the local step fingerprint as the child's complete identity.
Do not assert any arbitrary lexicographic ordering of digests.

Supplemental plan: docs/plans/derived-templates.md.
Verify current issue state with br show before claiming.
acceptance_criteria:
- The helper's byte contract is documented next to its implementation.
- Existing root tests retain their expected values.
- Composition tests pass with default and disabled default features.
- No raw fingerprint representation becomes public.
- The diff is limited to identity implementation, documentation, and tests.
close_reason: Implemented versioned framed SHA-256 parent/step composition; independent golden vector, parent/step/order/ancestry changes, and unchanged root vector pass in both feature modes. cargo test --locked --lib fingerprint; cargo test --locked --no-default-features --lib fingerprint; cargo fmt --all -- --check passed.

title: Derive immutable templates through shared acquisition
description:
Delivery epic: postgres-test-harness-j82.

# Derive immutable templates through shared acquisition

Type: feature.
Priority: 1.
Depends on: DT1 (postgres-test-harness-j82.1).
Unblocks: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3), DT4 (postgres-test-harness-j82.4), DT5 (postgres-test-harness-j82.5), DT6 (postgres-test-harness-j82.6).
Primary files: `src/harness.rs`, `src/fingerprint.rs` documentation;
`src/server.rs` only when needed for integration with existing internals.

Implement public `DatabaseTemplate::derive(&self, TemplateSpec, initializer)`
returning `Result<DatabaseTemplate>` with the exact root callback bounds:
`FnOnce(String) -> Fut` and `Fut: Future<Output = Result<(), BoxError>>`.
Do not require `Send`, `Sync`, or `'static` from caller initialization code.
The supplied spec identifies only the local delta.
Compose it with the parent's complete fingerprint using DT1 (postgres-test-harness-j82.1).
Use the parent's own server and project.

Extract one private async acquisition helper from `PostgresHarness::template`.
Roots supply their unchanged identity and source `template0`.
Children supply the composed identity and a private owned source descriptor
containing `Arc<TemplateInner>`.
Both methods share weak caching, local flights, PostgreSQL coordination,
recovery, initialization, sealing, error mapping, and publication.

Extend `begin_template` to use that descriptor.
Move a source owner into its actual blocking closure and hold it through
classified CREATE and Initializing metadata tagging.
Do not retain it solely in the outer future.
Do not add parent fields to `TemplateInitialization` or `TemplateInner`.
Do not execute `CREATE DATABASE` when the child is already ready in cache or
catalog; cloning an in-memory source handle before the lookup is harmless.

Continue using `create_managed_database_classified` and the existing target
lock protocol; only source selection changes.
Use the complete child fingerprint for naming, cache, metadata, and locks.
Keep metadata version one and root identity behavior unchanged.
Keep application callback execution on the calling task.
Template setup does not acquire downstream lease permits.
New CREATE operations still pass terminal database admission.

Document the difference between local spec and returned complete identity,
callback skipping on hits, retry after failure, and caller-managed inputs.
Document that aborted initialization can leave a recognized template for
retry/stale cleanup and is not covered by the disposable drain barrier.
Preserve existing abort error behavior, including combined callback/drop errors.

Include basic real-PostgreSQL tests with a populated root, child, sibling,
and grandchild.
Use distinct step SQL to create or change markers.
Assert exact contents from disposable clones, unchanged parent contents,
different identities when parent or step changes, and callback suppression
on warm acquisition.
Add a compile/unit test invoking the public method with a borrowed, non-Send
capture to guard the public callback bounds without requiring a live server.
Construct or type-check the future; do not execute database I/O in that test.

Acceptance:

- The public method compiles in both feature modes and on Rust 1.88.
- Roots and derived templates share one acquisition protocol.
- A child initializer sees inherited rows and a writable child URL.
- Parent, sibling, and disposable-clone isolation are observable in SQL.
- A grandchild inherits the child and ancestor identity.
- Warm child acquisition skips the supplied initializer.
- Existing root coordination and recovery tests still pass.
- No runtime dependency, metadata version, or public handle type is added.

Validation:

```console
cargo test --locked --lib
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --lib
cargo test --locked --doc
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --doc
cargo test --locked --test postgres derived_ -- --ignored --test-threads=1
```

Also run the existing template-focused ignored lifecycle regressions after
the shared-path extraction; include the full lifecycle suite at final feature
verification.

Why one shared protocol:
duplicating advisory-lock handoffs and failure cleanup would allow root and
child behavior to diverge in precisely the cases this harness manages.

## V02 — Changed inputs and ancestry

Owner: DT1 (postgres-test-harness-j82.1), with database-level confirmation in DT2 (postgres-test-harness-j82.2).
Setup: two parent identities and two local step identities.
Action: compose each relevant pair and then apply a fixed grandchild step.
Oracle: identical pairs remain stable; changed parent or step produces a
different child; changed child changes the grandchild.
Failure detected: ignoring the parent, using a shortened fingerprint, or
returning the local step fingerprint as the child's complete identity.
Do not assert any arbitrary lexicographic ordering of digests.

## V03 — Parent data reaches child callback

# Prove derived coordination and interrupted-build recovery

Type: task.
Priority: 1.
Depends on: DT2 (postgres-test-harness-j82.2).
Unblocks: epic completion.
Primary files: `tests/postgres.rs`; narrow unit test support in
`src/harness.rs` only if an ownership boundary cannot be gated externally.

Extend real PostgreSQL 18 tests for `DatabaseTemplate::derive`.
API: `derive<F, Fut>(&self, TemplateSpec, F) -> Result<DatabaseTemplate>`,
where `F: FnOnce(String) -> Fut` and
`Fut: Future<Output = std::result::Result<(), BoxError>>`.
There are no `Send` or `'static` callback bounds.
The spec identifies the local step; the returned fingerprint composes it
with the parent's complete identity.
The implementation uses a weak per-server cache and PostgreSQL target locks.
Initialization error/cancellation can be retried on a fresh parent copy.

Existing `tests/postgres.rs` anchors are `OwnedHarnessFixture`, `CatalogLock`,
`QueuedAdvisoryLock`, `TemporaryDatabase`, `advisory_key`,
`advisory_lock_is_acquirable`, `wait_until_advisory_lock_is_acquirable`,
and `wait_until_database_statement`.
Template keys use `advisory_key("template", &format!("{project}:{}",
fingerprint.to_hex()))`; the coordination domain is `template-coordination`.
Use `pg_database` plus `shobj_description(oid, 'pg_database')` for exact
catalog state and the version-one format documented in `src/metadata.rs`.
Do not introduce new metadata fields for test instrumentation.

For same-harness waiters, pin the acquisition future and poll it through a
test-side `std::future::poll_fn` wrapper.
Send a oneshot signal after the first Pending poll while the winner remains
gated, and await that signal before releasing/cancelling/panicking the winner.
Continue polling the same future; starting another acquisition would miss the
wakeup behavior being tested.
Use PostgreSQL lock observations for independent-harness waiters.

Prove same-harness concurrent callers share one successful initialization and
one retained child lock session.
Prove two independently started external harness handles targeting the same
server/project converge on the same child with only one successful setup.
Use SQL row effects as well as invocation counters; an in-memory counter
alone is not evidence of server coordination.
This independent-server-cache test is sufficient for the advisory protocol;
do not describe it as an actual separate-process test unless one is run.

For error, cancellation, and unwinding panic, write a unique partial marker
before interrupting the winning initializer.
Keep a waiter pending through a channel/catalog-confirmed stage.
Retry with a fresh initializer that asserts the partial marker is absent and
inherited parent data is present.
Verify the waiter completes and the parent still supplies correct clones.

Cover cancellation during blocking preparation using an observed child
coordination wait or a narrow test-only worker gate.
Abort the caller and await a join error with `is_cancelled()` while the worker
remains gated, drop all outer parent handles, and verify the parent's
exclusive advisory lock remains unavailable while the worker is gated.
Release the worker and verify its source lock can eventually be acquired.
Recover any resulting recognized child state without publishing partial data.

Cover abandoned finalization with a channel/catalog-confirmed gate after the
initializer has returned and before sealing completes.
Concretely, wait until the callback signals it has started, acquire the
existing `CatalogLock`, then release the callback to return success.
Observe the final Ready `COMMENT ON DATABASE` for the exact child on an active
backend with `wait_event_type = 'Lock'` and a confirmed catalog blocker.
Use `pg_blocking_pids` or expose the controlled `CatalogLock` backend PID in
the test fixture, and match `state=ready` in the statement.
The existing `wait_until_database_statement` matches last-query text alone;
do not reuse it unchanged as proof that finalization has reached this gate.
Cancel the caller and await `JoinError::is_cancelled()` before releasing the
catalog blocker, so the outer future's resources have actually been dropped.
Only read the child's comment after the blocker is released.
Allow the worker to complete after caller cancellation, then reacquire and
prove the successful step is not rerun when the catalog is Ready.
Do not require publication into the vanished caller's in-memory flight.

Verify stale cleanup can remove an eligible parent after all parent handles
are dropped while a child remains live; then query a fresh clone of the child.
Verify a child's own live lock protects it from that sweep.
Use a dedicated test project and
`cleanup_stale_databases(admin_url, project, Duration::ZERO)` so valid current
metadata is immediately eligible without timestamp rewrites.
Inspect exact parent and child names after the sweep.
Do not delete by prefix or manipulate unrelated databases.

Exercise a deterministic child-name collision with unrecognized metadata.
The database must remain intact and derive must return the existing
inconsistency error.
Also cover sealing with lingering child connections and confirm the parent
is never unsealed or targeted by termination.

Acceptance:

- Tests assert inherited/final/partial row states, not only success values.
- Races are ordered with signals or PostgreSQL observations, not fixed sleeps.
- Cancelling a waiter does not cancel the winning initializer.
- The detached worker keeps the parent protected and releases it afterward.
- Completed children retain no ancestor locks after outer handles drop.
- Ready metadata survives abandoned local publication and skips reinitializing.
- Unknown databases are preserved on deterministic-name collisions.
- Bounded timeouts produce useful lock/activity diagnostics on failure.

Validation:

```console
cargo test --locked --test postgres derived_ -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --locked --lib detached
```

If a required regression fails, fix the owning production path within this
bead's stated lifecycle contract and rerun the affected root regressions.
Do not weaken the oracle to match a broken implementation.

Why these tests are a delivery outcome:
they establish recovery and isolation guarantees under real server locks and
interrupted asynchronous work, beyond ordinary happy-path API coverage.

## V07 — Warm acquisition does not touch PostgreSQL

Owner: DT2 (postgres-test-harness-j82.2)/DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).

existing warm-template regression pattern.
Action: derive the same child with a callback that would return an error if run.

is still held; callback is skipped and no extra child lock session appears.

Release all external blockers through RAII on failure paths.

## V08 — Same-harness concurrent cold start

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: parent with stable rows and several child callers sharing one harness.
Action: synchronize their start and hold the winning callback long enough for
other calls to become waiters.
For each intended waiter, await the signal from its first Pending poll of
the pinned acquisition before allowing the winner to finish.
Oracle: all successful results name the same child; one initializer executes;
one shared child lock session remains while handles are held; final SQL rows
contain one setup effect.
Failure detected: key mismatch, duplicate flights, or duplicated permanent
lock sessions in a single server cache.

## V09 — Independent harness coordination

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: two `PostgresHarness::start` calls use the same server/project and
disable startup cleanup for the controlled race.
Acquire equivalent parent handles through each independent server cache.
Action: race child acquisition while the winner's callback is explicitly gated.
Oracle: loser does not enter its initializer; both return the same child;
database contents show one successful setup effect.
Failure detected: relying only on in-memory cache coordination.
Do not expect one shared-lock session across distinct harness allocations.

## V10 — Error retries start from a fresh parent copy

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: winning child callback writes a partial marker, then waits for release.
Start a waiting acquisition using the same parent and local spec.
Await its registered-Pending signal while the winner remains gated.
Action: release the winner with a known initializer error.
Oracle: caller receives that error; waiter later initializes; its first query
finds the parent's rows and no partial marker; final child rows are correct.
Failure detected: publishing partial state or resuming a delta on dirty data.
Combined cleanup errors must not discard the original initializer failure.

## V11 — Cancelled initializer wakes a retrying caller

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: winner writes a partial marker and signals that it is inside callback.
Start a waiter, await its registered-Pending signal, then abort and await the
winner's task.
Oracle: waiter eventually runs its own initializer against a fresh copy;
partial marker is absent and inherited parent data remains present.
Verify task cancellation explicitly from its join result.
Failure detected: flight owner not waking waiters, locks leaking, or dirty
initializing targets being treated as valid ready children.

## V12 — Panic recovery follows cancellation ownership

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: callback writes a partial marker, then panics after a release signal.
Action: register a Pending waiter, observe an unwinding task panic, and let
that same waiting acquisition retry.
Oracle: retry uses fresh inherited data without the partial marker;
the parent remains usable.
Failure detected: panic poisoning cache ownership or stranding target locks.
This test covers unwind-enabled test builds only.
Do not catch application panics in the production public API to satisfy it.

## V13 — Cancelling a waiter preserves the winner

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: hold the winning initializer behind a channel and start a second caller.
Await the second caller's registered-Pending signal.
Action: cancel the waiting caller, then release the winner successfully.
Oracle: winning callback completes once and a later acquisition reuses the
ready child without running another callback.
Failure detected: waiters accidentally owning or cancelling the shared flight.
No special cleanup should target the winner's database because a waiter left.

## V14 — Detached preparation retains the source

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: obtain a parent, arrange a target-lock wait observable in PostgreSQL,
then start derivation with an owned parent moved into a spawned task.
Action: once its blocking worker is demonstrably waiting, abort the async task
and await a cancelled join result while the gate remains held, then drop every
other parent handle.
Oracle while gated: attempting the parent's exclusive advisory lock fails.
Release the target blocker and await observable worker/session completion.
Oracle afterward: the parent lock is eventually acquirable, and recognized
child state can be recovered without wrong inherited rows.
Failure detected: passing only a source name into detached blocking work.

## V15 — Ready finalization survives abandoned publication

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: callback writes its complete marker and signals immediately before
return; hold finalization at a SQL-observable catalog write or test-only gate.
Acquire `CatalogLock` while the callback is still gated; release the callback;
observe the final Ready `COMMENT ON DATABASE` on the exact child from an
active backend with a Lock wait and confirmed catalog blocker.
Match `state=ready`; a session's last Initializing comment is not evidence.
Action: abort and await the async caller's cancelled join result while the
finalizer remains gated; then release the catalog blocker.
Oracle: catalog eventually shows Ready, with no child connections permitted;
reacquisition with an erroring callback succeeds without invoking it.
Failure detected: treating a lost in-memory publication as a need to rerun a
successfully sealed initializer.
The gate must be acquired after preparation, not before initial metadata tagging.

## V16 — Completed child survives parent reclamation

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: build a root and child in a dedicated project; retain only the child.
Action: wait for parent lock release and run owner-aware stale cleanup with
`Duration::ZERO`, using existing valid metadata without rewriting timestamps.
Oracle: parent disappears, child remains protected, and a fresh child lease
contains all inherited and child rows.
Failure detected: unnecessary persistent parent ownership or cleanup depending
on a durable ancestry graph.
Do not assume dropping a handle immediately drops its database.

## V17 — Unrecognized target remains untouched

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: determine an expected child name from a previously obtained identity
or the exact independent fingerprint recipe; create a controlled lookalike
with missing or foreign metadata and a marker proving ownership.
Action: request the corresponding derived template.
Oracle: inconsistency error, unchanged marker/database, callback not invoked.
Failure detected: unconditional replacement of a deterministic target name.
Clean only the test-owned lookalike using its RAII guard and exact name.

## V18 — Sealing terminates only lingering child clients

Owner: DT3 (postgres-test-harness-j82.3).
Setup: child callback retains a client connection using the existing held-client
fixture pattern and then returns success.
Action: await derivation and inspect child readiness and client termination.
Oracle: child is sealed and clonable, held child connection has ended,
and parent clones continue to show unchanged inherited state.
Failure detected: attempting to clone a source with active child sessions or
targeting the wrong database during sealing.

- Cancelling a waiter does not cancel the winning initializer.
- The detached worker keeps the parent protected and releases it afterward.
- Completed children retain no ancestor locks after outer handles drop.

title: S02: Resolve connection-limit overrides into one validated value
description:
## Verdict

title: S13: Revalidate stale databases after acquiring their lock
description:
## Verdict
Recommend as a concurrency/state correction. Audit rank 3. High impact and confidence; medium effort and blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/harness.rs:591 snapshots all database rows once.
- src/harness.rs:598-610 classifies snapshot records before locking.
- src/harness.rs:611-622 acquires the snapshot key, then drops and counts without rereading.
- src/admin.rs:324-330 uses DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS.

## Current complexity
A snapshotted Initializing template can become Ready or fresh before lock handoff. Metadata can move to another protecting key. Two sweepers can both count the same database after DROP IF EXISTS.

## Target
Treat the initial scan as a hint. After acquiring the candidate key, use S08-A's exact lookup, rerun the existing classifier, require the current key to equal the held key, and only then drop/count. Reuse CleanupClassification where practical; avoid parallel candidate/outcome type hierarchies unless needed for centralized unlock handling.

src/harness.rs plus the S08-A private admin lookup. Always release the originally acquired key on every path. Account for an extra query, disappeared/changed rows, error precedence, and observable CleanupReport counter changes.

1. Snapshot an old managed database as a cleanup candidate.
2. Keep its advisory lock held so the sweeper waits or skips before deletion ownership is authoritative.
3. Refresh/finalize the same resource, or let another sweeper delete it, before the original sweep acquires the snapshot key.
4. Observe that the current code drops/counts from the stale snapshot without an exact locked reread.

The locked reread is authoritative; a changed/fresh/ready/missing/key-mismatched database is not dropped or falsely counted; two sweepers cannot both report one drop; lock release and error paths are validated.

title: S09: Close connection admission on owned shutdown
description:
## Verdict
Recommend as a lifecycle correction. Audit rank 9. Medium impact, medium-high confidence, low effort, medium blast radius.

## Evidence
- src/server.rs:47-49 and 108-120 own the semaphore and permit acquisition.
- Error::ConnectionBudgetClosed exists at src/error.rs:95-96.
- src/server.rs:133-138 removes an owned container but never closes admission.
- PostgresHarness::shutdown(&self) at src/harness.rs:69-72 leaves clones available.

## Current complexity
Queued or later callers can receive permits after the owned server is removed and then contact a dead endpoint; the closed-budget error is unreachable.

## Target
Close the existing semaphore before terminal owned-container shutdown. External shutdown remains a no-op. Do not introduce a server state enum for this single transition.

## Scope and risks
src/server.rs and observable shutdown behavior. Decide and document whether failed container removal still makes admission terminal. Characterize active permits, clones, repeated/concurrent shutdown, and external mode.

## Validation
Saturate the budget, park a waiter, shut down, and require prompt ConnectionBudgetClosed. Add active-lease, repeated/concurrent, failed-removal, and external no-op cases.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure a budget that can be fully consumed by one live DatabaseLease.
2. Start a second database request so it waits on the semaphore.
3. Call owned PostgresHarness::shutdown while clones and the waiter remain.
4. Release the first permit and observe the waiter can be admitted only to contact the removed server instead of receiving ConnectionBudgetClosed.

## Acceptance Criteria
Owned shutdown closes admission and wakes queued permit requests with ConnectionBudgetClosed; external shutdown does not close admission; failure/repeat/concurrency semantics are documented and tested.
